finishes.note: Crema Marfil Coto, selected grade, 30 mm, laid in eight rings of radial slabs (sheet 3.3), mirror-polished through 3000 grit and a final compound (the Future's working); 6 mm joints, grouted in the stone's own dust in resin; the polish dulled in the walking lanes (door to landing, the ring round the landing). Includes the 30 mm lip at r 2.290.

The 6 m base: inner face r 14.000, the cove recess, the coping band, the wall top and the footing. Travertino Romano vein-cut, voids filled with tinted resin, polished (the palette's Future working for the Atrium's base only: the modern's last stone, under the glass). Ashlar coursed by Form, vertical joints on the rib lines and bay centres.

Outdoors: the plinth's exterior dress (base moulding, ashlar face r 14.880, coping cornice and wash), the equator entablature and the portal (block, opening, socle, cornice, architrave, keystone). Every exterior surface is travertine (Story: outdoors honed, then weathered).
The west door's rough opening through the base (hidden behind the joint's lining).
The floor slab r 2.560 ... 14.000, z -0.500 ... -0.030 (hidden structure; the palette's Future role for concrete).

The misty glass: inner leaf r 14.000 ... 14.024, 2 x 12 mm Optiwhite laminated on a UV-filtering interlayer; the room face acid-etched to a satin, the cavity face a white ceramic frit. Its visible transmittance is the Matter record's (measured), never a knob.
Outer leaf r 14.050 ... 14.074, clear heat-strengthened laminated Optiwhite; takes the museum's weather.

The Sphere's underside as seen from the Atrium: triangular panes, 2 x 12 mm laminated Optiwhite, the room face acid-etched in a light-extraction pattern; the diffusers of the edge-lit luminous ceiling (sheet 4). Room face R 14.024, upper face R 14.000.
The twelve ribs: S355J2, blast-cleaned, epoxy primer, oyster-white (RAL 1013) basecoat, mica interference pearl, satin clear coat.
The canopy grid (60 x 120 members), the compression ring round the car's way, its twelve hanger plates and the drum's head closer ring.
The collar round the car's way (the iris's housing): lathed body, coffered band and 24 spokes; 8.2 m across.
Outdoors: the drum's order (12 fins, 12 pedestals, 12 mullions, 3 transom rings); the same pearl build in fluoropolymer (Story: outdoors).
The rib shoes, sleeves 15 mm proud to z 0.360 (Story: rib shoes mirror-polished, lacquered).
The 24 mm line up each rib's face from the shoe to the ring (polish).
The ring you wait on (r 2.940 ... 3.060, flush) and the waiting mark west of it (half ring and dot, 2 mm proud in 10 mm recesses): mirror-polished, dulled where people stand (Story).
The bay letters A-K in the floor at r 13.100, 0.300 high, 2 mm proud in 10 mm recesses (polish); clean oil gilt.
The collar's gilt: the hub liner, the four tori at the rings' arrises and the lip band at the rim (Story: collar, gilt rim).
The collar iris's blades, their undersides as the Atrium sees them: oil gilt over the pearl coat (gilt on lacquer).
The collar iris's blades, their upper faces (seen from the Sphere's neck): pearl, as the palette's iris linings.
The landing's shoe and head ring and the tube's ring frame (cast CuSn10, oil gilt).
The curved sill across the landing door, set into the marble, bridging to the car's base ring: walked, so mirror-polished bronze, not gilt.
The landing enclosure (panes and leaves) and the tube to the collar: 15 mm toughened laminated Optiwhite, the edges' pale aqua showing at every joint.
The car's panes, leaves and clear roof: 15 mm toughened laminated Optiwhite.
The car's floor disc r <= 2.135, laminated, acid-etched anti-slip (Story: the car's frosted floor).
The car's glass handrail rod, 36 mm, ball ends.
The car's base and top rings, leaf fins, roller-guide blocks, crown and its four arms, handrail brackets (Story: gilt rings).
The Cube mast (spiral-band column clad in gilt), its head, and the under-floor seat where the Sphere's mast meets the car (Story: mast oil-gilt).
The lining through the slab r 2.300 ... 2.560, seen only from the shaft: the Cube's dark patina (Story: the one place the future is black, a light-field room must not reflect).
The two guide rails with the racks on their backs and their brackets: machined steel, ground and hard-chromed (ruled palette key); the lift's working steel, as real guide rails are.
The Starry Night's stele: 60 mm Optiwhite laminated from toughened plies, 1.500 x 2.140 visible.
The stele's foot, cast CuSn10 (Story: the stele foot mirror-polished, was brass).

The Starry Night's slim frame: the Salon's gilt profile at W 0.060, carved on a quartersawn oak core, gesso and red bole, burnished water gilding, clean (Story: the one oak in Élan, invisible). Art builds it.
Site's closed pair of cast CuSn10 leaves in the west class opening while atrium.west is unmated (the stand).
Site's blind for atrium.down while unmated: the class closure (iris.4600) shut on the mating plane z -0.500.
